program.title: BSc in Environmental Management and Technology
uncertain: The 'ENVR' course entry under Elective(s) with name 'All ENVR elective courses' and 0 credits is ambiguous—it may represent a placeholder for all ENVR electives, but no specific courses are listed. This needs clarification.

The course 'LANG 2082' and 'LANG 2083' appear to be split across lines in the PDF (e.g., 'Communication for Environmental Management and' and 'Technology I' on separate lines). The names were reconstructed as best as possible but may require verification.
The course 'LANG 3081' appears on page 2 with name split as 'Communication for Environmental Management and' and 'Technology III' on separate lines; reconstructed similarly.
The course 'MATH 1020' has credits_raw '3 4' suggesting a range, but the format is irregular—lower bound 3 used as per rules.

The course 'ECON Note: ECON 2103 OR ECON 2113' on page 2 was interpreted as a group-level note, but the individual courses ECON2103 and ECON2113 are listed immediately after—this may indicate the note applies to a choice, but since both are listed as separate courses, they are included as options. The note was attached to the group, but it's unclear if this was intended as a Fundamental Course note.

The 'Fundamental Course(s)' group includes a header row with 'COMP/ISOM' and a note, then lists COMP1021, COMP1022P, ISOM2010 as separate rows. It is unclear if students must take one from the note or if these are all options. The note says 'Note: COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P OR ISOM 2010', suggesting a choice of one, but all three are listed as separate courses. Per rule 4, the note is attached to the group, and each mentioned course is listed. This results in listing all three as available courses, which may overcount—human review needed to confirm if only one is required.

Similarly, the 'MATH' row has a note: 'Note: MATH 1003 OR MATH 1012 OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023' and lists each course separately. Same ambiguity: is one required or are all listed as options?
The total required credits for the major is not explicitly stated in the text, so it is set to 0 as per instructions.

total_required_credits (26.0) is a computed value: the sum of the required_credits of all groups in this file. The PDF does not state a single overall minimum total for this program, so this figure is derived by summation and may double-count where optional tracks/options are listed as separate groups.
